title: Microsoft Teams: manage call groups from Teams on Mobile
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap, the supplied Microsoft notice and Microsoft Learn. Its corrected admin paths, PowerShell commands, licensing and rollout description agree with those sources.

claims.claim: This roadmap change concerns managing call groups in Microsoft Teams on Mobile.
claims.quote: "title": "Microsoft Teams: Manage call groups on Mobile"

claims.claim: Users will be able to create and manage their call group directly from Teams on Mobile without switching to desktop.
claims.quote: Users can create and manage their call group directly from Teams on Mobile.

claims.claim: Mobile call group management allows users to add members.
claims.quote: They can add or remove members, configure how the group should ring

claims.claim: Mobile call group management allows users to remove members.
claims.quote: They can add or remove members

claims.claim: Users can configure how their call group rings from Mobile.
claims.quote: configure how the group should ring

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users can forward incoming calls to their call group from Mobile.
claims.quote: choose to forward or simultaneously ring incoming calls to their call group

claims.claim: Users can ring their call group at the same time as their own devices.
claims.quote: users can forward their calls to the group or ring the group at the same time as their own devices, using the call handling options in Calling settings.

claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on early December 2026

claims.claim: The cited Learn call group page has no mobile-specific management steps at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "Manage call group" "mobile" "policy". Read call-sharing-and-group-call-pickup in full: admin-center and PowerShell procedures, but no mobile management procedure.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Call groups share incoming calls with colleagues who can answer while the user is unavailable.
claims.quote: let users share their incoming calls with colleagues so that the colleagues can answer calls that occur while the user is unavailable.

claims.claim: The notice describes existing call group changes as requiring the desktop.
claims.quote: Call groups let colleagues answer calls on a user's behalf, but changing one today means going to the desktop.

claims.claim: The notice says no admin action is required before rollout.
claims.quote: No admin action is required before rollout.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The new Mobile screen reaches eligible users without admin enablement, supporting defaultState on.
claims.quote: Once available, eligible users will see Manage call group in the Calling settings of Teams on Mobile. ... No admin action is required before rollout.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Mobile uses the existing calling policy controlling call groups.
claims.quote: uses the existing calling policy that controls call groups.

claims.claim: Users with call groups turned off in their calling policy cannot use this Mobile feature.
claims.quote: If call groups are turned off for a user in their calling policy, they won't be able to use the feature on Mobile.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The notice makes the Mobile feature available to users with a Teams Phone licence.
claims.quote: This feature is available to users with a Teams Phone license

claims.claim: Learn requires a Microsoft Teams Phone licence to set up and use call sharing and group call pickup.
claims.quote: Users must be assigned a Microsoft Teams Phone license to set up and use call sharing and group call pickup.

claims.claim: The Mobile management experience is included in the Teams Phone entitlement already required for call groups.
claims.quote: This feature is available to users with a Teams Phone license and uses the existing calling policy that controls call groups.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The notice names no other licence, meter or charge for the Mobile management experience.
claims.quote: Searched: "manage call groups" "mobile" license price meter. Read MC1552390 and Learn call-sharing-and-group-call-pickup; the notice specifies Teams Phone but no additional licence, meter or charge.

claims.claim: The sources describe no new identity or permission for Mobile call group management.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "call groups" "mobile" "permissions". Read MC1552390, call-sharing-and-group-call-pickup and teams-calling-policy; no new Mobile identity or permission was described.

claims.claim: Be immediately forwarded makes incoming calls bypass the user's own devices.
claims.quote: Be immediately forwarded so that calls to the user don't ring their devices.

claims.claim: CallGroupTargets replaces existing membership with the full set supplied.
claims.quote: You need to always specify the full set of members as the parameter value. What you set here will overwrite the current call group membership.

claims.claim: A call group can have up to 25 users.
claims.quote: Each call group can have up to 25 users.

claims.claim: A user can own only one call group.
claims.quote: A user can only own one call group.

claims.claim: Adding more than five call group members automatically switches ring order to Everyone at once.
claims.quote: If you add more than five members to a call group, the ring order automatically switches to "Everyone at once."

claims.claim: Call group owners and members must be in Teams Only deployment mode.
claims.quote: Users, the call group owner, and members of the call group must be in Teams Only deployment mode.

claims.claim: The notice lists no additional admin prerequisite beyond the existing calling policy and Teams Phone licence.
claims.quote: This feature is available to users with a Teams Phone license and uses the existing calling policy that controls call groups. ... No admin action is required before rollout.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The calling policy control is at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Edit > Inbound calls can be routed to call groups.
claims.quote: select Voice > Calling policies. ... Select the policy or policies that you want to modify, and then select Edit. ... Inbound calls can be routed to call groups

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowCallGroups $true enables call groups in the specified calling policy.
claims.quote: -AllowCallGroups: Enables the user to configure call groups in the Microsoft Teams client and that inbound calls should be routed to call groups. ... Type: Boolean

claims.claim: Calling policies can be assigned to individual users or groups.
claims.quote: Assigns a specific Teams Calling Policy to a user, a group of users, or sets the Global policy instance.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: A user's group is accessible at Teams admin center > Users > Manage users > user > Voice > Call answering rules > Ring user's devices > Also allow > Group call pickup > Manage call group.
claims.quote: go to Users > Manage users and select a user. ... go to the Voice tab. ... Under Call answering rules ... Ring user's devices and select Group call pickup from the Also allow dropdown. ... Select Manage call group

claims.claim: Set-CsUserCallingSettings -Identity <user principal name> -CallGroupOrder InOrder -CallGroupTargets <array of sip addresses> sets the user's group members and ring order.
claims.quote:
$cgm = @("sip:user2@contoso.com","sip:user3@contoso.com")
Set-CsUserCallingSettings -Identity user1@contoso.com -CallGroupOrder InOrder -CallGroupTargets $cgm

claims.claim: The second control edits an individual user's existing call group rather than enabling or disabling the Mobile management screen.
claims.quote: This example shows how to update the call group of user1@contoso.com to add user5@contoso.com and remove user6@contoso.com.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; controls[2].api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate admin UI or API switch for Mobile call group management is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "Manage call group" "mobile" "policy"; "call group" "mobile" "Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy". Read call-group, calling-policy, settings-reference and both Set cmdlet pages; no separate Mobile switch found.

claims.claim: The notice explicitly says Mobile management uses the same controls as desktop.
claims.quote: Manage call groups on Mobile uses the same controls as the desktop experience.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn directs admins to clean up call group relationships in the Teams admin center when turning off call groups to avoid incorrect routing.
claims.quote: When you turn off call groups for users, you must clean up the call group relationships for users in the Teams admin center to avoid incorrect call routing.

claims.claim: Routing for PSTN calls set to Use unanswered settings takes precedence over call group forwarding and simultaneous ringing.
claims.quote: If Use unanswered settings or Send to voicemail is used, either of these settings will have precedence over other call forwarding settings like call forwarding with simultaneous ringing to delegate, call groups, or call forwarding.

claims.claim: Routing for PSTN calls set to Send to voicemail takes precedence over call group forwarding and simultaneous ringing.
claims.quote: If Use unanswered settings or Send to voicemail is used, either of these settings will have precedence over other call forwarding settings like call forwarding with simultaneous ringing to delegate, call groups, or call forwarding.
